title: Segmented fab: array-only line plus mature-node periphery wafer
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation resolves 'leading-edge cells vs cheap periphery': run only the ~25 array-critical layers in a slim array fab, build sense amps, drivers and I/O on a 28-40 nm logic wafer bought from idle U.S. foundry capacity, and join them by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding under the mats. The array fab no longer needs high-voltage, multi-Vt or logic-metal modules.
why: Periphery is ~49% of the die and ~15-20 masks; splitting cuts array-fab tool types ~30-40%, frees die area for cells (+40-60% bits/wafer) and lets U.S. foundries supply half the silicon (facts 4, 7; capital, U.S. manufacturability).

title: Matryoshka multi-shell capacitor contacted by etch-selective recesses
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting resolves 'more charge but no taller hole': ALD alternating TiN and Ru electrode shells separated by ZrO2 inside one hole, then a TiN-selective top recess and a Ru-selective bottom recess tie odd shells to the storage node and even shells to the plate, giving 3-4 parallel capacitor walls per hole.
why: Cs ~2-2.5x per hole at constant AR, so today's ~5 fF needs only ~30:1 instead of 60-75:1; removes 1-2 support-mesh masks and the slowest HAR etch tool-hours (facts 1, 4).

title: Merchant EUV template wafers sold to DUV-only memory fabs
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action resolves 'need EUV pitch but cannot afford EUV': a central hub pre-patterns the three densest periodic layers (active islands, buried wordlines, capacitor-hole hardmask) into a durable SiN/carbon hardmask stack on blank wafers and ships them to small fabs that finish every coarse layer on DUV, aligning to marks embedded in the template.
why: Each small fab avoids $200M+ per EUV scanner and most of the 5-7 EUV layers; the hub runs scanners at >90% utilization across customers, letting several U.S. memory fabs start at ~1/3 the capex (fact 4).

title: Disposable nanoimprint daughter templates for periodic array layers
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying plus #27 Cheap short-living objects: write one master template by e-beam, replicate hundreds of daughter templates by imprint, and run each daughter for ~1-5k wafers on jet-and-flash imprint tools for capacitor-hole and landing-pad layers, discarding it when defects accumulate while array redundancy absorbs the rest.
why: Imprint tools cost ~1/5-1/10 of an EUV scanner and ~1/10 the power; moving 2-3 of the 5-7 EUV layers to NIL cuts the litho cost of those layers ~40-60% (fact 4).

title: Anodic alumina self-ordered pores as the capacitor mold
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: instead of plasma-etching 70:1 holes, grow them - deposit ~1.5 um aluminium over the array, nano-indent or DUV-print a shallow pit lattice at the storage-node pitch, and anodize so pores self-propagate straight down at 100:1+; widen pores, open the barrier oxide, then ALD the electrode and dielectric.
why: Replaces the costliest HAR etch (high-power/cryo RIE, many chamber-hours) with a room-temperature electrochemical bath at <1% of the capex; aspect ratio becomes nearly free, so Cs can rise toward 8-10 fF (facts 1, 4).

title: Dose-encoded single EUV exposure patterns two layers at once
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: expose wordline trenches at full dose and contact openings at half dose in one EUV pass on a dual-threshold resist stack; develop and etch the high-dose features first, then trim the resist to uncover the half-dose features for a second etch that is self-aligned by construction.
why: Removes one EUV exposure and one overlay error per merged pair; merging 2 of 5-7 EUV layers cuts EUV cost per wafer ~25-35% and tightens overlay (fact 4).

title: Three-beam interference lithography for all dense hexagonal array layers
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: one maskless tool interfering three 193 nm beams at 120 degrees prints the honeycomb lattice for active islands, capacitor holes and landing pads by only changing phase and rotation; spacer doubling brings it to ~40 nm hex pitch and a cheap DUV block mask trims the array edges.
why: No reticle and simple optics: tool cost perhaps 1/20 of EUV and 1/5 of an immersion scanner, and ~3-4 masks disappear from the flow (fact 4).

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching drills capacitor holes at wet-bench cost
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution replaces the ion field with a catalytic chemical one: pattern a noble-metal catalyst dot lattice, immerse in HF/H2O2, and each dot sinks vertically into silicon carving 100:1 holes for buried capacitors or vertical-channel transistors, 50 wafers per batch.
why: Wet bench ~$1-3M vs ~$5-10M+ per HAR etch chamber plus chillers; batch processing raises deep-etch throughput ~10x (fact 4, capital).

title: 1D-only design rules: every critical layer is lines and cuts
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: make the cell tight in one direction only - active, wordline and bitline are pure line/space gratings by self-aligned quadruple patterning on DUV, all 2D information comes from cut masks at 3-4x pitch, and storage nodes are segments formed where two SAQP gratings intersect.
why: 1D gratings print on DUV at 20-24 nm pitch with high yield; removes EUV holes and pads (~5 EUV exposures) at ~10% cell-area penalty (fact 4).

title: Double-sided wafers: memory arrays on both front and back faces
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: finish a front-side array plus periphery, bond face-down to a carrier, thin to a 1-2 um etch stop, then build a second transistor/capacitor array on the backside of the same active layer, reaching the shared front periphery through nano-TSVs.
why: Doubles bits per starting wafer, halving CZ silicon and high-purity quartz crucible use per bit and sharing one periphery for two arrays (~20-25% die-cost cut; scarce resource, capital).

title: Defect-absorbing soft-remap arrays that tolerate cheaper patterning
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: make the address map flexible instead of the process perfect - each 1 Mb mat carries ~3% spare rows/columns and an on-die CAM that remaps failing 64-cell groups at test and in the field, so the fab can run older ArF immersion scanners with ~1.5x worse overlay and accept cell-defect rates near 1e-4.
why: Older DUV tools and relaxed overlay specs cut litho capex ~50% on several layers and lift yield; ~3-5% area buys the tolerance (facts 4, 7).

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium sponge as the storage-node electrode
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: deposit a Ru-Al alloy into a shallow ~10:1 hole, then selectively dissolve the Al so spinodal dealloying leaves a 5-10 nm-ligament Ru sponge; conformal ALD ZrO2 and TiN then coat it, multiplying surface area 5-10x without a tall hole.
why: Trades aspect ratio for internal porosity: 5 fF in a hole ~1/4 as deep, deleting the HAR etch and support-mesh steps (facts 1, 4).

title: Helium-free etch: hydrogen backside cooling plus closed-loop recapture
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out separates the needed property (wafer-to-chuck heat conduction) from the scarce substance: switch electrostatic-chuck backside gas from He to H2 or H2/Ar where process-tolerant, and fit remaining He users with membrane plus cryogenic recapture loops reclaiming >90% of backside and purge flow.
why: Qatar's ~30% of helium has been offline since March 2026; fab He use drops 70-90%, removing a shutdown risk for etch and ALD tools (scarce resource, throughput).

title: Ballroom-free fab: ISO-1 microenvironments inside an ISO-7 shell
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter changes moves cleanliness from the building to the wafer: sealed FOUPs, nitrogen-purged EFEMs and tool-integrated ISO-1 microenvironments carry all contamination control, while the building is a cheap ISO-7 warehouse with ordinary HVAC.
why: Cleanroom shell and HVAC are ~20-30% of fab construction cost and set much of the 3-5 year build; could cut shell capex ~50% and time-to-first-wafer by ~1 year (capital).

title: Reusable donor wafers via porous-silicon release of device layers
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: only the top ~1 um needs device-grade crystal, so grow a double-porous Si release layer on a premium CZ donor, epi the device layer, bond it to a cheap reclaimed or multicrystalline handle, split at the porous layer and re-polish the donor for 10-20 reuses.
why: Cuts premium CZ wafer demand ~10x per bit, easing the Spruce Pine (>80%) quartz-crucible chokepoint, and gives a natural etch stop for backside processing (scarce resource, capital).

title: Self-grown landing pads by selective epitaxial overgrowth
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: let exposed silicon active tips grow their own landing pads - after bitline spacers form, selective Si:P epitaxy with faceted lateral overgrowth fills each storage-node contact and mushrooms to pad size, stopping at the spacer walls, so no landing-pad lithography is needed.
why: Deletes the landing-pad EUV/SAQP layer (one of 5-7 EUV exposures) and its overlay error; ~10-15% EUV cost cut (fact 4).

title: Supercritical-CO2 release deletes capacitor support-lattice masks
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics: replace liquid mold-strip and drying, whose capillary forces topple tall pillars, with anhydrous mold removal and supercritical-CO2 drying; with zero surface tension, freestanding 80-100:1 pillars survive without SiN support meshes.
why: Saves the 1-2 support-lattice litho/etch steps per capacitor module and permits taller pillars (Cs toward ~7 fF) (facts 1, 4).

title: Photopatternable hafnium-oxo resist that becomes the functional film
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes (change a substance's properties): use a Hf/Zr oxo-cluster resist that, after exposure and development, is annealed straight into dense HfO2/ZrO2 that stays as a hardmask, spacer or isolation layer, so the patterned film is never etched.
why: Collapses deposit-coat-expose-etch-strip into coat-expose-develop-anneal, saving ~3-4 steps per use and some etch chambers (process steps, tool cost).

title: Spatial ALD carousel boosts dielectric deposition throughput tenfold
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: replace pulse/purge temporal ALD with wafers rotating under gas-curtain-separated precursor and oxidant zones, so every revolution is one ALD cycle; ZrO2/Al2O3 capacitor dielectrics and liners deposit ~10x faster near atmospheric pressure.
why: ALD is a large share of capacitor and 3D-module tool count; ~5-10x wafers/hour per tool cuts ALD capex and footprint proportionally (throughput, capital).

title: Precursor cryo-trap recovery returns hafnium and ruthenium to suppliers
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: ALD uses only ~1-10% of its metal-organic precursor, so fit each ALD/CVD exhaust with a cold trap or adsorbent cartridge that captures unreacted Hf, Zr, Ru and Mo compounds, shipped back to the supplier for re-purification in a closed loop.
why: 50-80% metal recovery lowers precursor cost and Ru supply risk and lightens abatement load (scarce resource, cost).

title: Etch passivation engineered to become the contact insulating liner
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: the sidewall passivation that storage-node-contact etch deposits (normally stripped by wet cleans) is tuned with SiCl4/O2 into a dense 2-3 nm SiOx-rich film and kept as the contact-to-bitline insulating liner, skipping the separate liner ALD and spacer etch.
why: Removes ~2-3 deposition/etch/clean steps per contact module and the cleaning damage to fine features (process steps).

title: Self-calibrating sense amplifiers let periphery use relaxed transistors
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: each sense amp stores its own offset on its bitline capacitance during a pre-sense calibration phase, and a per-mat trim register is updated at power-up, raising tolerable Vt mismatch from ~10 mV to ~40 mV.
why: Lets periphery use cheaper, higher-variation transistors (fewer halo/Vt implant masks, mature-node periphery wafers) and shrinks SA area (fact 7, capital).

title: Millisecond flash anneal crystallizes high-k after periphery is built
idea: TRIZ #21 Rushing through: a 1-3 ms xenon flash or laser anneal heats only the surface ZrO2/TiO2 dielectric above 900 C, forming high-k tetragonal/rutile phases (k ~45-80) while underlying periphery and metals stay below ~500 C.
why: Higher k holds Cs at ~half the aspect ratio, and the capacitor can be built last (after periphery or bonding), removing protective layers and steps (facts 1, 4, 10).

title: Token-sweep restore: inference reads replace refresh, shortening capacitors
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: in LLM-inference memory every weight row is activated once per decode step (~10-16 ms) and each activation restores the cell, so the controller disables refresh and guarantees the sweep period; if serving pauses beyond the bound it drops the weights and reloads them from flash, keeping refresh power exactly zero.
why: Zero refresh power and bandwidth (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth today); a guaranteed ~16 ms window vs 64 ms cuts required Cs ~3x, so capacitor AR falls from ~70:1 to ~25:1, deleting support-mesh masks and halving HAR etch time (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Ephemeral-grade dies: retention-failing DRAM sold for TTL-bounded data
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: dies that fail the 64 ms retention screen but hold data for 4-8 ms are sold as E-grade parts with refresh logic fused off, and the runtime places only data with a hard time-to-live below the rated window (collective-communication buffers, prefetch staging, pipeline handoffs), invalidating pages at expiry.
why: Zero refresh power; recovers the ~3-8% retention yield loss and skips the long hot retention-pause tests that dominate DRAM test time (~20-30% test-cost and tester-capex cut) (facts 3, 4).

title: 77 K memory tier lets fabs drop recessed-gate access transistors
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter changes: run memory racks in liquid-nitrogen immersion, where thermally activated junction and subthreshold leakage fall by >20 orders of magnitude and only tunneling remains, so low-field planar cells hold charge effectively indefinitely while cold and refresh is switched off; the fab then builds simple planar or shallow-fin access transistors instead of the 3-4 mask buried-channel module.
why: Zero refresh power; ~8-10% fewer process steps and relaxed gate-layer patterning, plus higher mobility at 77 K; the ~10 W-wall-per-W cooling overhead is offset by removing refresh and leakage and denser racks (facts 3, 4).

title: Work-function-asymmetric electrodes make ZrO2 capacitors nonvolatile antiferroelectrics
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: keep the existing DRAM cylinder capacitor module but swap the top electrode for a conductor ~1 eV higher in work function (e.g., RuO2), creating a built-in field that shifts one antiferroelectric double loop to straddle zero bias, giving two remanent polarization states read through the same 1T1C sense path.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh, with AFE ZrO2 endurance ~1e11-1e12; converting an existing DRAM fab needs one electrode change and no new tool types, so capex is near zero vs a new fab (facts 3, 4).

title: Coaxial gallium-oxide 2T0C cell grown inside one vertical hole
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: in a 3D-NAND-like stack of word planes, one DUV-printed hole receives nested ALD shells at each tier recess - an outer amorphous Ga2O3 write channel gated by the plane, a metal storage-node ring, a thin dielectric, and an inner Ga2O3 read channel gated by that ring.
why: Ga2O3's 4.8 eV gap gives off-current below ~1e-21 A, so retention exceeds years and refresh is zero with no capacitor module; one hole mask serves 32-64 tiers, raising density without EUV (facts 2, 3, 4).

title: Stiction-latched nanopillar relay built with the capacitor-hole etch
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: use the existing 70:1 mold etch to free-stand a ~20 nm TiN pillar between two side electrodes; a pull-in pulse snaps its tip onto one electrode where van der Waals adhesion (stiction, normally a yield killer) holds it at zero power, and the read senses which side conducts.
why: Zero refresh and zero standby; a ~1 um pillar resonates at ~20-50 MHz, giving ~10 ns switching; reuses DRAM's own HAR etch and ALD tools so conversion capex is small, with no dielectric-leakage spec at all (facts 3, 10).

title: Twin tunnel-diode latch grown where the capacitor used to be
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging joins storage and restoring in one element: epitaxially stack two Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes in a short ~5:1 hole above the access transistor; their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages, and with sub-pA peak current the node self-latches (TSRAM-style).
why: Zero refresh power, with hold power ~0.05 pW/bit vs ~0.7 pW/bit for refresh today; the 60-75:1 capacitor module and its masks are replaced by low-AR epitaxy (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Silicon-carbide refresh-free memory in idle EV power-device fabs
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: the same 150/200 mm 4H-SiC lines that make EV MOSFETs (overbuilt in the U.S. as EV demand slowed) produce 1T1C memory, since SiC's 3.26 eV gap suppresses thermal generation so strongly that SiC MOS storage cells have shown retention extrapolating to years at room temperature.
why: Zero refresh, built on existing U.S. i-line/DUV tools with near-zero new capex; density is ~50-100x below DRAM, so it serves persistent, edge and high-temperature tiers and frees mainstream DRAM for hot data (U.S. manufacturability, capital).

title: Planar AlScN ferroelectric capacitor replaces the 70:1 pillar
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: alloying ~25-30% Sc into AlN makes a wurtzite ferroelectric with remanent polarization ~80-110 uC/cm2 (4-5x HZO), so a flat 30x30 nm, ~10 nm-thick AlScN capacitor sputtered on the storage contact switches ~1.5-2 fC, matching a 5 fF pillar's signal, using PVD tools U.S. BAW-filter fabs already run at volume.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; eliminates the HAR capacitor module (~20-25% of array steps) and its etch capex; endurance (~1e6-1e8 today) must improve or be buffered by an SRAM write cache (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Resonant-tunneling InAs/AlSb floating gate from compound-semiconductor fabs
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: a triple-barrier InAs/AlSb heterostructure is opaque at rest (AlSb ~2.1 eV conduction offset) but turns transparent when ~2.5 V aligns its resonant level, letting electrons enter or leave an InAs floating gate fast and at low energy while retention is non-volatile (ULTRARAM-type), grown on Si by MBE/MOCVD.
why: Zero refresh; switching energy per area ~100x below flash and demonstrated endurance >1e7; uses U.S. III-V epitaxy capacity instead of DRAM fabs and needs no HAR capacitor; the endurance gap is covered by write buffering (facts 3, 4).

title: Conducting domain-wall memory in lithium-niobate-on-insulator wafers
idea: TRIZ #32 Changing properties: in thin-film LiNbO3 (made by smart-cut for photonic modulators) a voltage pulse writes a nanodomain whose inclined wall conducts while the bulk insulates; reading measures wall current non-destructively and the domain persists without power.
why: Zero refresh and non-destructive read (no restore energy, cf. fact 8); a planar two-electrode cell patterned by DUV in a dedicated back end reuses the LNOI photonics supply chain, with 1e10-class endurance reported (facts 3, 4).

title: Sliding-ferroelectric 3R-MoS2 channel as a refresh-free 1T cell
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: store the bit as the stacking order (AB vs BA) of a wafer-scale CVD-grown bilayer 3R-MoS2 channel; a gate pulse slides the layers by one bond length, flipping out-of-plane polarization and shifting threshold voltage, which persists without power and without mobile ionic defects to fatigue.
why: Zero refresh in a 1T cell (~4F2 possible) with no capacitor module; sliding switching breaks no bonds, so endurance could exceed HZO FeFETs, and growth below ~500 C fits any BEOL (facts 2, 3, 4).

title: Expire-and-regenerate pages: let cells decay, recompute on miss
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: disable refresh entirely; each DRAM page carries a write timestamp, and any page older than its guaranteed retention counts as discarded, so reading it traps to the runtime, which regenerates the data from source (re-decompress weights from flash, recompute activations from checkpoints, refetch KV from a cheaper tier).
why: Zero refresh power; because regeneration is rare for hot data, the fab can target ~10 ms retention instead of 64 ms, cutting required Cs ~3x and with it capacitor height, etch time and support masks (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Elapsed-time-aware sensing reads decayed charge without refresh
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: instead of holding charge constant, make the read reference follow it - each row stores a few-bit write-epoch tag, and the sense reference is stepped down along the measured decay of matched reference cells written at the same time, keeping cells readable ~10x longer; paired with a page time-to-live, refresh is never issued.
why: Zero refresh; ~10x usable retention lets the fab cut Cs or accept a leakier, cheaper access transistor (drop a halo/channel implant mask, shallower buried gate) (facts 3, 4).

title: Base-array mask ROM with one e-beam-written via layer
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: pre-build generic NOR-ROM wafers (4F2 transistor arrays, DUV plus SAQP, ~25 masks, no capacitor) in bulk; once a model is frozen, program its weights by e-beam direct-writing a single via layer with two via sizes per bit-pair (2 bits/cell), so inference weights live in silicon with zero refresh and zero standby.
why: Weights are most of inference memory; ROM cost per bit could be ~3-5x below DRAM (no HAR capacitors, no EUV, ~40% fewer masks), frees DRAM for KV and activations, and maskless customization avoids per-model mask sets (facts 3, 4).

title: Vertical-channel 6T SRAM built on the 4F² DRAM transistor process
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: reuse the vertical-channel transistor module being developed for 4F2 DRAM, add a complementary p-type pillar, and wire six vertical transistors as a cross-coupled latch in ~24-30F2, skipping the capacitor module entirely.
why: Bistable, so zero refresh; ~5x denser than logic SRAM (~0.004 vs ~0.021 um2/bit) and built in DRAM fabs without the capacitor module (~20-25% fewer steps); ~4x less dense than DRAM, so it targets hot refresh-heavy tiers (facts 3, 4).

title: Vacuum-gap floating gate: field-emission writes, no oxide to wear
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere (vacuum): replace a floating gate's tunnel oxide with a sealed ~3-4 nm vacuum gap formed by sacrificial-layer release; writes use Fowler-Nordheim field emission across vacuum at a few volts, and with no dielectric there are no traps to generate, while the ~4.5 eV vacuum barrier keeps charge non-volatile.
why: Zero refresh with endurance no longer oxide-limited; a planar 1T cell with no HAR capacitor, using MEMS-style release and sealing already common in U.S. MEMS fabs (facts 1, 3, 4).

title: Floating-body 1T cells revived for millisecond-lived pipeline buffers
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: rather than fight floating-body retention (why 1T-DRAM failed), embrace it - build SOI or stacked-Si floating-body cells with ~10-100 ms retention and use them only for data overwritten every few ms (pipeline-parallel handoff buffers, double-buffered GEMM tiles, network rings), with refresh logic removed.
why: Zero refresh; the cell is a single transistor with no capacitor module (~25% fewer array steps, no HAR etch) and stacks readily into 3D (facts 2, 3, 4).

title: Self-selecting chalcogenide crossbar on a former 3D XPoint toolset
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out removes both the separate selector and the phase change: a single amorphous chalcogenide layer whose threshold voltage memorizes the polarity of the last pulse acts as selector and bit at once, built with 2 DUV masks per deck on a toolset like the one that ran 3D XPoint in Lehi, Utah.
why: Nonvolatile, so zero refresh; 4F2 per deck with stacked decks, no transistor or capacitor per bit and no EUV, reusing U.S. crosspoint know-how; ~1e9-1e10 endurance needs write buffering (facts 2, 3, 4).

title: Protonic three-terminal transistor holds state as pumped ions
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics treats ions as a working fluid: a gate pulse pumps protons from a hydrogenated reservoir through a solid electrolyte into a WO3 channel, changing its conductance; removing the field freezes the ions, so the state is nonvolatile and read non-destructively through a separate channel path.
why: Zero refresh and non-destructive read (fact 8); BEOL-compatible below ~300 C with sputter/ALD only, so it is capital-light with no EUV; ns-scale protonic switching has been reported, but endurance and hot retention are the risks (facts 3, 4).

title: Legacy-fab conversion fund for drop-in zero-refresh memory
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: a CHIPS-style program pays conversion costs plus a 5-year offtake for U.S. 200/300 mm legacy fabs (65-180 nm lines with idle tools) to run a standard refresh-free memory PDK (asymmetric-electrode AFE capacitor or self-selecting crosspoint), keeping depreciated tools productive instead of building new $15B fabs.
why: Conversion ~$0.2-0.5B per fab vs $15B+ greenfield; adds U.S. zero-refresh memory supply in ~18-24 months and offloads refresh-hungry DRAM (capital, U.S. manufacturability).

title: Antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bits pack densely with no stray fields
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight (counterweight): each bit's antiparallel magnetic sublattices counterbalance, so cells emit no stray field and can sit edge-to-edge; spin-orbit torque from a heavy-metal line switches the noncollinear antiferromagnet in sub-ns, an antiferromagnetic tunnel junction reads it, and retention needs no power.
why: Zero refresh; the stack is ~4-6 sputtered layers vs ~15-20 for a perpendicular MTJ, with no pinned reference layers, easing deposition and etch and allowing DUV-pitch crossbars; small readout signal is the risk (facts 3, 4).

title: Sixteen layer-transferred DUV tiers replace EUV shrink for density
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation moves density into height: transfer a ~50 nm single-crystal Si film per tier by smart-cut, build only an ~8-mask DUV array tier of planar nonvolatile cells (e.g., 6F2 at F~40 nm with asymmetric-electrode AFE capacitors) at <=500 C with laser dopant activation, and repeat 16 times above one shared periphery.
why: Zero refresh; 16 tiers at ~0.0096 um2/bit give ~0.0006 um2/bit effective, beating 1b-node DRAM (~0.00086) with zero EUV; capex shifts from scanners to cheap repeated DUV and bonding modules (facts 2, 4).
